rationale.conceptual: The paper's EnvisION simulation is a custom multi-component model combining ion single-scattering MC, secondary electron generation/transport with angular-dependent escape, SE-I/SE-II classification, and precursor gas kinetics. Implementing it requires translating several non-trivial physics sub-models (Bethe stopping, TPP-2M IMFP, Langmuir isotherm) into a coherent 3D simulation with solid-vacuum boundary crossing. Several interacting pieces must be integrated correctly, demanding careful algorithmic design.
rationale.execution: The task consists of two sequential simulation runs of the same codebase, each producing a single CSV file. There is no multi-stage data processing, no external data acquisition, and no complex dependency orchestration; a single script with standard scientific libraries suffices.

difficulty.reasoning: Implementing the full EnvisION Monte Carlo simulation from scratch is a non-trivial coding task that combines ion single-scattering Monte Carlo, angular-dependent secondary electron generation/transport with TPP-2M inelastic mean free path, and Langmuir gas kinetics. The method is customized and multi-component, requiring domain understanding, but the verification is lenient (only directional trends). The pipeline is simple: two runs of the same code producing two CSV files, no external tooling or data fetching.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The Monte Carlo simulation is CPU-bound, with modest memory for a 3D grid of deposited atoms (voxels on the order of nanometers, pillar heights ~150 nm) and particle-state arrays; no large datasets or GPU are required.
